answer: Memory-hard sequential proofs bind each identity to 2,400 RAM-bound hashes. An attacker needs 40,000 separate 4-GB RAM allocations because each identity requires 90 seconds of sequential memory work that resists parallelization. The network enforces this via on-chain verification of the memory-bound chain. The fable registry anchors enrollment, the dawn attestation log records each proof, and the crystal checkpoint finalizes penalties.
